clue.text: Deliveries shown up as best or worst?

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries bowled from one end
to show up is to come, and 'come' is also the past participle, as in 'has come'

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator wonders whether the deliveries shown on the replay were the bowler's best or worst.
explanation.walkthrough: 'best' and 'worst' look like superlatives describing the bowling, but both are verbs here meaning to get the better of someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To best or to worst an opponent is to defeat them, which is a synonym.

clue.text: Paint stains first to be removed

indicators.note: first to be removed says the opening letter of the word for stains is dropped

parts.note: to soil is to stain or dirty

explanation.surface: Paint stains need removing first.
explanation.definitionFit: Oil colours are a form of artist's paint, a synonym.

clue.text: Money we'll soon need? Regret raising none

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising means the word for regret is read upwards

parts.note: to rue is to regret
O is zero, or none

explanation.surface: Someone regrets that soon we will need money but have none.
explanation.walkthrough: In 1999 Britain was debating joining the single European currency.
explanation.definitionFit: The single European currency, which Britain was expected to adopt when the clue appeared.

clue.text: Reptile messing up clean home

indicators.note: messing up means disordering, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A reptile makes a mess of a clean house.
explanation.definitionFit: A colour-changing lizard is an example of a reptile.

clue.text: Drink blended wine and rare malt

indicators.note: blended means mixed together, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A drink of wine blended with rare malt whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'malt' suggests whisky, but the answer is something far tamer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottled spring water is an example of a drink.

clue.text: Cannon ball

definitions.meaning: a ... is a small automatic quick-firing gun
a ... is also a small woolly ball, as on a hat

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are dictionary meanings: a quick-firing naval gun and a decorative woollen tuft.

clue.text: Bulb lit up repeatedly, one having been plugged in

indicators.note: plugged in means inserted, so the letter for one goes inside the doubled word
repeatedly means the word for lit up is given twice

parts.note: a light that is lit is on
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A light bulb keeps lighting up once it has been plugged in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bulb' and 'lit up' suggest a lamp; the bulb is a vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: This vegetable grows as a bulb, an example.

clue.text: Mum or Dad restricting Irish boy's diet

indicators.note: restricting means confining, so the parent word holds the boy's name

parts.note: either is a parent
Liam is a common Irish boy's name

explanation.surface: A parent controls what their Irish son eats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diet' looks like food; it is the old word for a legislative assembly, as in the Japanese Diet.
explanation.definitionFit: A diet is a formal assembly of lawmakers, like the national legislature.

clue.text: One can never reckon a miss is a hit!

definitions.text: One can never reckon a miss is a hit!

parts.words: One can never reckon a miss is a hit!
parts.note: reads as about a poor shot, but a miss is a young woman and a hit is a success, so this person never rates any woman

explanation.surface: A marksman can never claim a miss counts as a hit.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman-hater would never think a young lady a success.

clue.text: Cross part of France?

parts.note: read as an angry region of France, but it names the region whose double-barred cross was the Free French emblem

explanation.surface: Which part of France is in a bad mood?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' seems to mean angry; it is the noun, the Cross of Lorraine, the two-barred cross adopted by de Gaulle's Free French.
explanation.definitionFit: A region of north-eastern France that also gives its name to a famous heraldic cross.

clue.text: High water, as cruiser leaving East set out

indicators.note: set out means arranged afresh, so the remaining letters are rearranged
leaving says the letter for East departs from the word cruiser

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: A cruiser leaves the East and sets out on high water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes E out of CRUISER, giving CRUISR, which 'set out' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloud of this type is made of ice crystals high in the sky, so it is water at great altitude.

clue.text: Liking forecast about end of rainfall before start of evening

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the forecast word goes round the two letters

parts.note: a prediction is a forecast

indicators.note: before places the rainfall letter ahead of the evening letter
end of picks the last letter of the word rainfall
start of picks the first letter of the word evening

explanation.surface: Someone fond of the weather forecast about rain ending before evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of rainfall' gives L and 'start of evening' gives E, which go inside PREDICTION.
explanation.definitionFit: A partiality or fondness for something is a synonym of liking.

clue.text: Very distressing tendency in court proceedings

indicators.note: in tells us the word for tendency sits inside the word for court proceedings

parts.note: a hearing is a session of a court case
a trend is a general tendency or drift

explanation.surface: A worrying tendency in the way court cases are run is very distressing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something heartbreaking, causing great sorrow, is a synonym.

clue.text: Agent providing someone who'll be paid to look after museum?

parts.note: a pro is a professional, someone paid for work
a curator is the person who looks after a museum's collection

explanation.surface: An agent supplies someone who'll be paid to manage a museum.
explanation.definitionFit: In Roman times and in some legal systems this officer acts on another's behalf, as an agent does.

clue.text: One might find HM's action right, however wrong

definitions.text: One might find HM's action right, however wrong

indicators.note: however wrong suggests something done badly, so the preceding letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters H, M and S taken as they stand

explanation.surface: A loyalist will defend the sovereign's actions as right, however wrong they are.
explanation.walkthrough: HM is Her Majesty, the sovereign; the whole clue both defines the loyalist and gives the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporter of rule by a king or queen would back the sovereign regardless.

clue.text: Greater honesty partly seen between Swiss banks — up to a point

definitions.text: between Swiss banks — up to a point

indicators.note: partly seen says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: More honesty is only partly seen between Swiss banks, to some extent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swiss banks' suggests secretive finance, but these are riverbanks.
explanation.definitionFit: This river rises in a Swiss glacier and flows through Switzerland before entering France, so only part of its course has Swiss banks.

clue.text: Boy at home cuddling girl — they enjoy courtship

parts.note: a lad is a boy

indicators.note: cuddling means wrapping round, so the word for at home holds the girl's name

parts.note: in means at home, as in 'staying in'
Esme is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A boy stays at home cuddling his girlfriend, and such people enjoy courting.
explanation.definitionFit: Men who enjoy the company of women and courting them are womanisers or charmers.

clue.text: Punitive females could make us men die after end of torture

indicators.note: after places the anagram behind the letter from torture
end of picks the final letter of the word torture
could make says the following letters can be rearranged into something new

explanation.surface: Avenging women could make us men die after torturing us to the end.
explanation.walkthrough: These are the Furies of Greek myth, euphemistically called 'the kindly ones'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Furies were female spirits of vengeance who punished wrongdoers.

clue.text: Armour's protruding part protecting a fellow, say?

indicators.note: protecting means guarding all round, so the word for the protruding part encloses the a

parts.note: the chin is the protruding part of the face

indicators.note: say signals that a word is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: a male is a man or fellow

explanation.surface: A piece of armour with a jutting part that protects a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' tells you MALE is heard as MAIL, the metal mesh.
explanation.definitionFit: Interlinked metal rings worn as body protection are a type of armour.

clue.text: Ghost's lots of long hair

definitions.meaning: in Roman religion the ... are the spirits of the dead, so a departed soul is meant
a mane is a long growth of hair on a horse or lion, or a person's thick hair

explanation.surface: A ghost has plenty of long flowing hair.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word for spirits of the dead coincides with the plural of a horse's neck hair.

clue.text: Engineers attending offensive smell that's recurring

parts.note: RE is the abbreviation for the Royal Engineers of the British Army
crude means vulgar or offensive
a scent is a smell

explanation.surface: Army engineers notice an offensive smell that keeps coming back.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaking out again after dormancy, as a disease may, is the meaning, a synonym.

clue.text: Sub supposedly superior, cricketer catching nothing

parts.note: U stands for upper class, the supposedly superior social set

indicators.note: catching means holding inside, so the cricketer word grips the zero

parts.note: a bat is a batsman in cricket
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A sub thinks they are better than a cricketer who catches nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sub' suggests a substitute player; it is a submarine.
explanation.definitionFit: A German submarine is an example of a sub, short for submarine.

clue.text: One's submerged in rubbish as a result of disorder

indicators.note: submerged in means placed inside, so the letter for one goes into the rubbish word

parts.note: rot is nonsense or rubbish
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone is sunk in rubbish because of disorder.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent public disturbance is a form of disorder.

clue.text: Fever making one unclear — very disconnected, initially

indicators.note: disconnected says the letter for very is cut off, and initially says it goes from the front

parts.note: vague means unclear

explanation.surface: A fever leaves a person muddled and very disconnected at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making one' links the definition to the wordplay; VAGUE loses its opening V.
explanation.definitionFit: This old word names a malarial fever with shivering fits.

clue.text: Support auxiliary returning after expedition

indicators.note: after places the reversed auxiliary behind the word for expedition

parts.note: a trip is a journey or expedition

indicators.note: returning means the auxiliary word is read backwards

parts.note: do is an auxiliary verb, as in 'I do know'

explanation.surface: A supporting assistant comes back after a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'auxiliary' suggests a helper or reserve; it is the grammatical auxiliary verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-legged stand holds up a camera, so it is a kind of support.

clue.text: Sticks, perhaps, fish next to kidney

parts.note: kidney means sort or kind, as in 'people of that kidney'
a ling is a sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A fishmonger displays a fish next to some kidney.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kidney' looks like offal; it is the old sense of temperament or sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Small dry sticks used to start a fire are an example of this firewood.

clue.text: Go round gallery, right round, starting at the front

indicators.note: starting at the front puts the letters for right and round ahead of the gallery

parts.note: O is round in shape
the Tate is a London art gallery

explanation.surface: Visitors go round the gallery, right round, starting at the entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn on an axis is to spin or revolve, a synonym.

clue.text: Liqueur in tea drunk put in

indicators.note: the final in says the word for put goes inside the rearranged letters
drunk means tipsy and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: to set something is to put it down

explanation.surface: Someone has put liqueur in their drunken tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges IN TEA to ANITE, and the final 'in' puts SET inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An aniseed-flavoured sweet spirit drink is a liqueur, an example.
